text:
andrew: Hey team — getting lots of 429s from our app hitting the authenticated streaming endpoint (POST /v1/streams/generate). Spikes happen at minute boundaries, ~15-25 requests suddenly 429. Example request_id: req_7b2f9c21. Using long-lived tokens reused across devices. Can someone help triage?

lia: Thanks Andrew — can you paste an example request (headers + minimal body) and let us know if this is via SDK or direct HTTP/2 streams? Also which region and client_id?

andrew: Direct HTTP/2 streams from mobile clients in us-west-2. Client id: acme-android-42. Example curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --http2 -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-stream-1","input":"...","stream":true}'
```
We reuse the same token on ~50 devices per customer and open a fresh stream per user action.

matt: Quick checklist: are the 429s RPM or TPM? Do you see them clustered at the top of the minute? From the request_id you gave I pulled logs: in that 60s window rpm=137, tpm=612. Our configured per-client RPM limit for that tier is 100, TPM 1000, so RPM spike looks like the culprit (requests/starts per minute). Long-lived streams count on start until they close.

juna: Root cause hypothesis: bursty stream creation near minute boundary + token reuse means many connections start simultaneously and count toward RPM. Streaming starts are rate-limited (start events), whereas the steady token bandwidth isn't the limiter. Mitigations:
- Reuse a single HTTP/2 connection and multiplex multiple logical sessions instead of opening N new connections at once.
- Stagger stream start times across clients with a small random jitter (e.g., uniform 0-2s) so starts don't align to the minute.
- Implement jittered exponential backoff on 429s. Example backoff stub: ```sleep = min(60, 2**attempt * (0.5 + rand()))```

lia: For immediate relief we can temporarily uplift RPM for your client while you deploy fixes. If this is a steady pattern, we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) or a quota bump on a recurring basis. Which do you prefer?

andrew: Appreciate it. Can you correlate the logs for client acme-android-42 around 2024-11-30T15:12Z and confirm how many distinct stream starts were counted? We'll roll out staging changes to reuse connections. Also please apply temporary uplift.

matt: I pulled inflight/start metrics: `api.stream.starts{client_id="acme-android-42"}` showed 142 starts in the 60s window you flagged. Inflight streams (concurrent open streams) was ~48. That matches the RPM breach. Also check that clients aren't leaving idle streams open; idle streams still count toward inflight slots until closed.

juna: Additional customer checklist: ensure clients send periodic keepalive pings only if needed (idle streams holding slots hurts start-rate), verify HTTP/2 multiplexing library settings (max concurrent streams per connection), and add client-side leaky-bucket to limit starts/second.

lia: Temporary uplift applied as requested: +40 RPM for 1h. Monitor and LMK if you need longer. :thumbsup:

ratecap-bot: Uplift applied: client=acme-android-42, delta_rpm=40, duration=3600s, by=lia

andrew: Thanks all — we'll ship stagger + connection reuse in the next deploy and monitor. Will follow up if 429s persist.

lia: Sounds good — ping me the rollout PR and I'll keep the uplift open until you confirm the drop in start-rate.
